\multicolumn{8}{p{\dimexpr\tblwidth-6\tabcolsep\relax}}{\scriptsize $^{*}p<0.05$, $^{**}p<0.01$, $^{***}p<0.001$; ns: not significant at $q<0.05$. $d$ is Cohen's $d_{z}$ (mean difference over the SD of those differences) on the paired cells and standard Cohen's $d$ (df-weighted pooled SD) on the 5 Welch cells. The capacity-matched grid comprises $60$ cells (six baselines $\times$ five datasets $\times$ two shots) and all 60 of them are corrected in one BH-FDR family. After the $n\geq20$ power extension the only unequal-count cells are the Proto-GAT rows (SpikeRPGNN $20$ runs vs Proto-GAT's $5$ on Tier-1 5-shot and DD/Rdt-M5k 1-shot), so those 5 cells use Welch's test. They are retained rather than dropped: excluding them would shrink the correction family and make every surviving $q$-value smaller, which is the direction that flatters the proposed method. Both accuracies of every cell are reported in Table~\ref{tab:main_results}.}
